issue: M60 relationship-ontology wave — CLJ-D57 (R7 placeholder endpoints)
note: A def-family form with NO NAME — or with a LITERAL in name position — defines nothing, so it may publish no symbol, no `contains` edge and no `exports` edge. `(s/defn)` in clj-kondo's `corpus/schema/defs.clj` published a symbol literally called `unknown` plus a `contains` edge into it, and CLJ-D53's `exports` edge inherited the same name: two edges whose endpoint was a placeholder literal, found by the ontology census at `contains 1 placeholder / exports 1 placeholder` over 633 corpus files. The symbol itself was already dropped further downstream by `keepSymbol`'s UNIVERSAL denylist in `src/ast/pool-worker.ts`, which is why the production symbol table looked clean while two edges did not — a filter that reaches symbols and not edges. CLJ-D35 ruled the same way for `(s/fdef 1 :args)`. The control at the bottom is what makes the sweep falsifiable: a form that DOES name something must still declare it, or `drop every nameless def` would satisfy every forbid below.
